parts.notes: Official MAD CAD, not a mock. Converted from mad-8318-ipe.stp (Creo, 2024-07-11) pulled from MAD's own product page 2026-08-08; source kept at cad/reference/mad8318/. Ø91.5 x 41.000 exactly. Stator-base end: Ø17.8 recess ~3 deep with a Ø3.0 bore at centre - this is what the j1_rotor_magnet_carrier's Ø2.85 peg engages. Ø5.0 bore runs right through. Hub end: Ø13.0 bore, Ø29 hub ~2.7 proud. NO protruding shaft either end.
J1 rotor eccentric: hub flange (PA6-CF). Countersunk M3 on BCD20 + M4 on BCD23 into the 8318 hub; 4x M3 heat-set inserts on BCD26 receive the cartridge.
Journal cartridge: 15.06 journal at e=+1.2 spans z78.4-87.6, engaging stock disc 1 via the stock 15x28x7 bearing. Base disc spins inside the case's 38.2 pilot.
Journal-2 cap at e=-1.2 spanning z87.6-96.8 (stock disc 2 plane). Spigot register + 2x countersunk M3 down into the cartridge; separate piece so each bearing slides on from its own end.
Printed retention washer over the disc-2 bearing race; M3 into the cap pilot.

J1 motor cage shell v2: case-pilot register + stock M5 square; O96 bore, 2.5mm wall, bayonet channels+seats at the bottom rim, small high vents. v1 radial-screw joint replaced after load-path review: cyclo eccentric reaction (~500N radial) now crosses a full-circumference bayonet instead of 4 screws in a slotted 1.75mm tube.

Magnet-bridge shaft blocker: stock O55 bolt interface (5x O6 measured positions), 3-spoke bridge, 6x5 diametric magnet pocket opening down toward the tray-pedestal AS5047P (~1mm gap). Grown 3mm downward; screws counterbored. Replaces the stock open-hole blocker; rides rotary_base.

Stock Main base with an O103 relief pocket about the cyclo axis (world 75.63,-87.66): full radius z 14-67.5, 45-deg roof to r44 by the case-fan seat (z 74.33). The MAD 8318 (O91.5) + cage skirt (O101) overrun the stock wall face 45.0 mm from that axis - discovered on the bench 2026-08-02 after the first PETG base print. Verified fits vs this mesh: shell 0.91, floor 1.48, motor 5.73 mm. Thinnest remaining wall 2.4 mm beside the stock wire window; boolean watertight, 7.7 cm3 removed. Bake this into every arm - do NOT print the stock Main base.

Stock cyclo output shaft with a relief pocket in its underside, about the cyclo axis. The shaft is SOLID through the middle - no bore - so the j1_cap (O15.06 x 11.2) and j1_washer (O18.06 x 2.5) that retain the eccentric cartridge had nowhere to go and were holding the shaft ~4 mm proud of the disc stack: the top 623 of each output-pin span ran in air (3 of 4 engaged) and the washer, which turns at motor speed while the shaft turns at 1/15, ground on the shaft's flat face. Caught on the bench 2026-08-07, fixed part on the arm 2026-08-08 and confirmed working. SIZING: the binding constraint is the BC28 mounting circle, inner edge r12.58 - NOT the BC46 pin holes at r21.65. Cap and washer both sit on axis (offset 0.02 mm) so they spin but never orbit; clearance covers print tolerance only. This file is O21 x 6 (1.47 mm clearance, 2.08 mm wall, verified against every hole at 12 depths). Arm 1 was built with an earlier O24 cut leaving 0.58 mm of wall - harmless in practice, because the 36T pulley's M3x15 only reaches z=14.8 and the shaft blocker's M3x10 z=19.8 while the thin wall lives in z 0-6, so nothing threads within 8.8 mm of it. Arm 1 stays as built; arms 2 and 3 print this O21 version. Boolean watertight, bounds identical to stock, drops straight in. Do NOT print the stock output shaft. JOURNAL: the Ø50.2 upper boss is ALSO turned down to Ø49.80 in this file. Stock is Ø50.17 against the 6810's Ø50.00 bore - 0.17 mm interference by design, and PETG's +0.10..0.30 print oversize takes that to 0.27-0.47 mm, which will not go on by hand. Found on the bench 2026-08-08 as a gap at the top-cover/main-case seam plus galling marks on the boss. Ø49.80 designed lands at Ø49.9-50.1 real - slip to light press. DEPTH: pocket deepened 6 -> 10 mm on 2026-08-08. The first cut cleared the washer (2.5) but not the M3 CAP HEAD sitting on top of it (3.0) - 5.5 mm of stack into a 6 mm pocket, which print tolerance eats. 10 mm gives 4.5 mm clearance. Depth is cheap here: the 36T pulley's M3x20 tips stop at z=18.14, so 8.14 mm of solid material remains below them, and the core inside BC28 is not in the torque path from the pins to the mounts. Bench workaround for an already-printed 6 mm shaft: swap the washer screw to an M3 BUTTON head (1.65 vs 3.0 tall) - drops the stack to 4.15 mm.

Stock rotating-base J1 output shaft with its Ø50 column journal (z 0-49.2) turned down to Ø49.80. Stock is Ø50.07 against the two column 6810s' Ø50.00 bore - interference before printing, same failure mode as the cyclo shaft boss but milder. Turned down 2026-08-08 alongside it so both 6810 journals on the arm share one fit spec. Ø21.8 wire bore and all hole patterns untouched; boolean watertight, 851 mm3 removed. Placement TBD - not yet positioned in the twin.
Fused encoder disc + motor strap rev D: planks to the alcove rack channels, 5x M3 into the post columns (3E/2W).
AS5047P breakout mock (30.33 sq, chip up). Board top against the pocket ceiling at world 25.43; chip looks up through the O12 window at the rotor magnet.

open_issues: Motor cage CAD landed 2026-07-29 (cad/j1/). Main base 8318 relief landed 2026-08-02 (cad/j1/stl/main_base_8318.stl). Output shaft relief pocket landed 2026-08-08 (cad/j1/stl/j1_output_shaft_pocket.stl). Still to design: bulged Joint 1 cover (interior must clear O101 on y), base electronics tray.

BENCH-FOUND 2026-08-09, bake for arms 2/3: the 4 cage-shell screws use the stock Joint 1 main case's NEMA 46.92-square holes FROM THE CHAMBER SIDE, but only the stock design's own positions are counterbored - our screw heads stood proud on the chamber floor at r~33 and pinched whichever cyclo disc was lowest (bottom-disc-only pinch, diagnosed by disc-swap + witness marks). Arm 1: counterbores hand-drilled. Arms 2/3: regenerate the main case with 4x counterbores (M3 cap: O6.5 x 3.5 / M5 cap: O9 x 5.5) at the cage screw positions before printing.

parts.notes: Petar's FAZE4 mount: disc bolts to the J6 output flange, beam carries the gripper body.
Chassis. Feature-derived pose 2026-07-29: jaw pivot holes (local x23,y+/-18.5) -> group (24.6,+/-18.5,56); drive-gear bore (45.6,-36) -> (19.75,-35.9,33.4); plate spans group x -11..11.
Drive jaw on the gear-side pivot (-y). Pivot bore mapped onto the body's pivot hole; arm extends +z to the finger root at z97.
Driven jaw on the +y pivot; sector gears mesh at y=0 (pivot spacing 37mm = the sector pitch diameter).

TPU finger, drive side. Roll corrected 2026-07-29: slice data shows the tip tapers to y~1.5 so the straight GRIP face is the y-min edge - now facing the centerline. Root socket lands on the arm end at (24.6,-18.5,97).
TPU finger, driven side, mirror of flex_1 with grip face inward; root at (24.6,+18.5,97).
55T final gear on the body's drive bore (28.5mm to the drive-jaw pivot), axis = plate normal = group x.
Compound 36T + pinion behind the plate on the drivetrain axis.
Planet carrier tucked inside the planetary cover envelope on the drivetrain axis.
12T planet at ~10mm orbit radius inside the cover (x3 in the real unit).
Planetary bearing plate on the plate back.
Planetary cover on the plate back, drivetrain axis.
Retainer plate over the jaw pivots.
MAD 5010 (factory STEP) pancake on the drivetrain axis behind the plate - replaces the underpowered gimbal motor; new motor plate is an open design item. Grip force = S1 current limit.
